stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved when running on Apple Silicon via Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance, specifically using the Aider polyglot benchmark, shows up to a 90% speed increase.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage for LLMs.
The updates also lead to higher quality outputs from the language models running on the platform.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, leveraging Apple's native ML framework.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and speed.
The core value proposition is bringing powerful AI capabilities to the user's personal device rather than relying on cloud services.

stories.title: Big Tech accused of stonewalling European social media researchers
stories.author: Anna Desmarais, wired.com
bullet_points: Major tech platforms (TikTok, X, Meta) are facing accusations of obstructing data access.
The core issue is that these companies are allegedly failing to provide data legally mandated for European social media researchers.
This highlights ongoing regulatory friction between Big Tech and European data governance requirements.

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation of current 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in handling complex 3D spatial reasoning tasks.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework that integrates both implicit and explicit 3D geometries derived from RGB videos.
Features Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) designed to embed high-level geometric priors into the VLM architecture.

stories.title: GraphVid: Interactive Graph-Controllable Video Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: GraphVid addresses the challenge of precise multi-object interaction control in video generation.
It overcomes limitations of text prompts and trajectory-based controls, which struggle with complexity and occlusion.
The system utilizes a graph-based approach to enable flexible and accurate control over multiple subjects in generated videos.

stories.title: Beyond Sycophancy: Structured Resistance and Compliance in LLM Moral Reasoning
stories.author: Bernard Koch
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of simply reducing LLM sycophancy by proposing a more nuanced understanding of social calibration.
The core finding is that LLMs need to learn to distinguish between incorporating external perspectives and maintaining independent, well-grounded moral judgment.
The study identifies three structured dimensions governing how models revise their judgments in response to others.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: Introduces OpenForgeRL, an open-source framework designed to train AI agents end-to-end.
Addresses the difficulty of training agents that rely on complex, stateful inference harnesses (like Claude Code/Codex) using standard open infrastructure.
Enables the training of harness-native agents across diverse environments, bridging the gap between complex reasoning and open-source training stacks.

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of 2D-based Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in handling complex 3D spatial reasoning tasks.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework that integrates both implicit and explicit 3D geometries derived from RGB videos.
Employs Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) to enhance the model's high-level geometric understanding.

stories.title: DONDO: Open w2v-BERT Speech-Recognition Base Models for African Languages
stories.author: Paul Azunre
bullet_points: Introduction of DONDO, a family of open, permissively licensed ASR base models specifically for African languages.
The models utilize the w2v-BERT 2.0 self-supervised speech encoder and cover 27 language varieties across several African nations.
Training data primarily consists of read speech from religious texts, ensuring broad and license-clear usage.

stories.title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
stories.author: Alagappan Valliappan
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical scaling issue in speculative decoding when using Multi-Token-Prediction (MTP) draft heads.
The core problem is that MTP draft heads incur a linear cost with context length due to full attention over the KV cache.
The proposed 'Windowed-MTP' aims to mitigate this 'Full-Context Draft-KV Tax' to maintain efficiency at million-token contexts.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models and hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The new feature set also includes web search capabilities for Claude Code.
This enhances the functionality of local LLM deployments via Ollama.

stories.title: Apple is banking on privacy to set its smart glasses apart
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly planning to unveil its first smart glasses at WWDC next June.
The expected consumer launch timeline for the smart glasses is set for the end of 2027.
Apple is prioritizing the development and messaging of strong privacy features to differentiate its product.

stories.title: SpaceX eyes tower catch for next Starship after auspicious end to 13th flight
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: SpaceX plans to attempt a tower catch for Starship on its next flight.
This follows a successful conclusion to the 13th Starship flight.
The maneuver indicates continued focus on refining Starship recovery procedures.

stories.title: Anthropic's Opus 5 is about token efficiency, not a capability leap
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Anthropic's Opus 5 update emphasizes token efficiency over massive capability gains.
The article suggests that current, more cost-effective AI models are often sufficient for practical use.
This points to a market trend where efficiency and cost-effectiveness are becoming as important as raw performance in LLMs.

stories.title: Roku raises streaming stick prices by up to 60 percent
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Roku is significantly increasing the prices of its streaming sticks by up to 60%.
The company attributes the price hikes to a shortage of RAM.
The news contrasts with a recent positive outlook from the CEO regarding the business.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for explaining time-series classifiers.
Addresses a limitation in current methods by incorporating 'necessity' alongside 'sufficiency' in explanations.
Aims to prevent spurious subsequences from being over-emphasized in model explanations, aligning with counterfactual reasoning.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent reasoning capabilities across different input modalities (text vs. visual diagrams).
The study highlights that different views of the same problem can elicit different behaviors in VLMs, suggesting incomplete or fragmented reasoning.
The research introduces 'MIRROR' to address this by learning from complementary views for improved multi-modal reasoning.

stories.title: Expanding Flow Maps
stories.author: Pranam Chatterjee
bullet_points: Introduces 'Expanding Generative Flows' (EFlows) to address limitations in existing flow-based generative models.
EFlows allow for generation across distributions of increasing dimensionality by augmenting the state with conditional noise.
The research aims to overcome constraints related to fixed dimensions or fixed sequence lengths in current generative models.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for explaining time-series classifiers.
Addresses a limitation in current methods by incorporating 'necessity' alongside 'sufficiency' in explanations.
Aims to prevent spurious subsequences from being over-weighted in model explanations, aligning with counterfactual reasoning.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent reasoning capabilities across different input modalities (text vs. visual diagrams).
The study, MIRROR, suggests that different views (text, diagram, combined) expose complementary, yet sometimes conflicting, reasoning paths in VLMs.
This highlights a current limitation in multimodal AI, where strong text reasoning does not guarantee equivalent visual reasoning.

stories.title: X$^3$-OPD: Distilling Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models via On-Policy Alignment
stories.author: Tao Jin
bullet_points: Addresses the gap in deep logical reasoning capabilities of large audio-language models compared to text-based LLMs.
Introduces X$^3$-OPD, a cross-modal on-policy distillation framework.
The framework transfers advanced reasoning skills from a powerful text teacher model to an audio-language student model.

stories.title: The Boundaries of Automation: A Theory of Persistent Human Participation
stories.author: Iryna Gurevych
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing assumption that human involvement in AI is solely due to current system limitations.
It shifts the focus from 'how far automation can extend' to identifying the conceptual limits of automation.
The research posits that human participation may remain necessary even when AI systems achieve high levels of capability.

stories.title: MedGame: Storytelling Gamification Empowered by Large Language Models for Medical Education
stories.author: Qi Dou
bullet_points: Introduces MedGame, a framework that gamifies medical education using LLMs.
Addresses a gap in current LLM medical tools by moving beyond single-turn Q&A to structured, decision-centered learning trajectories.
Utilizes a dual-engine design, including a Medical Narrative Designer, to transform static clinical cases into interactive games.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: Introduces OpenForgeRL, an open-source framework designed to train AI agents end-to-end.
Addresses the difficulty of training agents that rely on complex, stateful inference harnesses (like Claude Code/Codex) using standard open infrastructure.
Enables harness-native agents to be trained across diverse environments, simplifying the integration of complex reasoning and tool use.

stories.title: GS-Agent: Creating 4D Physical Worlds With Generative Simulation
stories.author: Chuang Gan
bullet_points: The research focuses on generating dynamic and physically realistic 4D worlds directly from natural language descriptions.
It addresses the limitations of traditional computer graphics, which require extensive manual effort for fine-tuning.
The core challenge being tackled is ensuring physical plausibility and controllability in generative simulation models.

stories.title: What, Where, and How: Disentangling the Roles of Task, Language, and Model in Code Model Representations
stories.author: Piotr Wilam
bullet_points: The research investigates how different language models (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and DeepSeek-Coder-V1-6.7B) represent code concepts across two languages (Python and Rust).
It uses a 2x2 design to disentangle the influence of the specific task, the programming language, and the underlying model architecture on code representation.
The study measures a comprehensive inventory of grammatical concepts to determine if representations are consistent across different model/language combinations.

stories.title: Agentic coding without the cloud: evaluating open-weight large language models on longitudinal data preparation tasks
stories.author: David Bann
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy and governance limitations of using cloud-based LLMs for coding tasks involving sensitive data.
Proposes using locally deployable, open-weight LLMs as a viable alternative for on-premise AI agent development.
Introduces an open-source framework to evaluate the effectiveness of AI agents in longitudinal data preparation tasks.

stories.title: Tracing a multi-agent LLM system: otel-swarm and a SigNoz dashboard pack
stories.author: himanshu_748
bullet_points: Addresses the complexity of debugging multi-agent LLM systems, which is harder than single LLM calls.
Introduces 'otel-swarm' as a tool/framework for tracing these complex multi-agent interactions.
Utilizes a SigNoz dashboard pack for visualization and monitoring of the tracing data.

stories.title: Claude Code Cost Control in Production: Token Budgets, Caching Strategies, and What the Billing Dashboard Hides
stories.author: jsmanifest
bullet_points: Focuses on practical, real-world challenges of managing operational costs when using Claude for code generation in production environments.
Discusses specific technical strategies like implementing token budgets and caching to optimize API usage.
Highlights the need for deeper insight into the billing dashboard to accurately control and predict LLM expenses.
